The story strikes a very natural and effective balance between scene and summary/exposition. It is primarily anchored in a real-time scene—the conversation between Ilse and Jonas on the ferry, punctuated by immediate sensory details (the cyclist paying the fare, the fog over the river, the wet shoes, the physical actions of securing the ramp). Woven seamlessly into this present-moment scene are brief, poignant moments of exposition and summary that provide crucial backstory without halting the pacing. For instance, the narrative briefly summarizes Jonas's childhood habit of hiding discomfort, and uses the physical object of Henning's boots to deliver the exposition that Henning has been gone for three years and Ilse has been pushing his boots aside every morning since. Because the exposition is directly triggered by the characters' real-time observations and actions, the story remains vivid and emotionally engaging while still delivering all the necessary background information to make the final gesture—Ilse offering the boots to Jonas—resonate deeply.
